finding.claim: Unauthenticated OS command injection in GET /ping: req.query.host is concatenated into a string passed to exec(), which runs it through /bin/sh, so an attacker can run arbitrary commands as the server user.
finding.source: tools.js:6 - req.query.host from the unauthenticated GET /ping query string

trace.note: Route /ping registered with no auth middleware; req.query.host is attacker-controlled
host concatenated unvalidated into shell command string passed to exec()
Command stdout returned to attacker via res.send(out), giving direct output
app.listen(3001) with no host argument binds all interfaces, so the route is network-reachable

finding.guards_checked: No validation, allowlist or regex on host; no authentication or authorization middleware on the route; exec used instead of execFile so no argv-safe separation; Express query parsing does not sanitize values (array/object values still concatenate into an injectable string). No enforced control found on the path.

verdict.reason: tools.js:6 registers GET /ping with no auth middleware, tools.js:7 concatenates the unvalidated req.query.host into a string passed to exec() (which runs through a shell), tools.js:11 returns stdout to the caller, and tools.js:28 calls app.listen(3001) with no host so it binds all interfaces; an anonymous remote attacker can inject shell commands and read the output.
